questions.question_text: A dataset has $Q_1 = 18$ and $Q_3 = 30$. What is the upper fence for identifying outliers?

options.why: Added 1 x IQR (12) instead of 1.5 x IQR (18) to Q3.
Added 1.5 x IQR to Q1 instead of Q3 (18 + 18).
Multiplied Q3 directly by 1.5 instead of adding 1.5 x IQR.

questions.question_text: A dataset has $Q_1 = 24$ and $Q_3 = 36$. What is the lower fence for identifying outliers?

options.why: Subtracted 1 x IQR (12) from Q1 instead of 1.5 x IQR (18).
Subtracted 1.5 x IQR from Q3 instead of Q1 (36 - 18).
Calculated 12 - 18 instead of 24 - 18.

questions.question_text: The five-number summary for a dataset is $\text{Min} = 4, Q_1 = 15, Q_2 = 22, Q_3 = 31, \text{Max} = 58$. Using the formal $1.5 \times \text{IQR}$ rule, which of the following is true?

options.text: $58$ is an outlier because it is greater than the upper fence of $55$.
$4$ is an outlier because it is less than the lower fence of $5$.
options.why: Calculated the lower fence incorrectly; the lower fence is 15 - 24 = -9, so 4 is not an outlier.

options.text: Both $4$ and $58$ are outliers.
options.why: Assumed both extreme values are outliers without evaluating the lower fence correctly.

options.text: There are no outliers in this dataset.
options.why: Failed to compare the maximum of 58 against the upper fence of 55.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{IQR} = 31 - 15 = 16$
$\text{Lower fence} = 15 - 1.5 \times 16 = -9$
$\text{Upper fence} = 31 + 1.5 \times 16 = 55$
Since $58 > 55$, $58$ is an outlier.
Since $4 \ge -9$, $4$ is not an outlier.

questions.question_text: A set of $10$ scores is: $2, 20, 21, 23, 25, 26, 28, 30, 32, 35$. Given $Q_1 = 21$ and $Q_3 = 30$, determine which value, if any, is an outlier.

options.text: $2$ is an outlier.
$35$ is an outlier.
options.why: Tested 35 against Q3 + IQR (39) incorrectly; the upper fence is 43.5.

options.text: Both $2$ and $35$ are outliers.
options.why: Assumed both the minimum and maximum must be outliers.

options.text: There are no outliers.
options.why: Did not calculate the lower fence (7.5) to test the minimum score of 2.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{IQR} = 30 - 21 = 9$
$\text{Lower fence} = 21 - 1.5 \times 9 = 7.5$
$\text{Upper fence} = 30 + 1.5 \times 9 = 43.5$
Since $2 < 7.5$, $2$ is an outlier.

questions.question_text: A dataset of runner times has $Q_1 = 44\text{ s}, Q_3 = 56\text{ s}$, with minimum $30\text{ s}$ and maximum $70\text{ s}$. Are there any outliers?

options.text: No, all data values lie within the fences of $26\text{ s}$ and $74\text{ s}$.
Yes, $70\text{ s}$ is an outlier.
options.why: Subtracted 1.5 x IQR from 56 instead of adding to find the upper fence.

options.text: Yes, $30\text{ s}$ is an outlier.
options.why: Calculated the lower fence as 32 s by using 1 x IQR instead of 1.5 x IQR.

options.text: Yes, both $30\text{ s}$ and $70\text{ s}$ are outliers.
options.why: Assumed the minimum and maximum must always be outliers without checking fences.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{IQR} = 56 - 44 = 12$
$\text{Lower fence} = 44 - 1.5 \times 12 = 26\text{ s}$
$\text{Upper fence} = 56 + 1.5 \times 12 = 74\text{ s}$
Since $\text{Min} = 30 \ge 26$ and $\text{Max} = 70 \le 74$, there are no outliers.

questions.question_text: In a modified box plot, how are outliers displayed, and where do the whiskers end?

options.text: Outliers are plotted as individual points beyond the whiskers, and whiskers end at the most extreme non-outlier data values.
Whiskers extend to the lower and upper fences, and outliers are plotted at the fences.
options.why: Whiskers extend to actual data values, not to theoretical fence boundaries.

options.text: Outliers are omitted entirely from the display, and whiskers extend to the minimum and maximum.
options.why: Outliers must be displayed as individual points rather than omitted.

options.text: Whiskers always extend to the minimum and maximum values regardless of whether outliers exist.
options.why: In a modified box plot, whiskers stop at the last non-outlier data value.

questions.solution_text:
A modified box plot plots any data value outside the fences ($Q_1 - 1.5\times\text{IQR}$ and $Q_3 + 1.5\times\text{IQR}$) as an isolated point.
The whiskers extend to the most extreme data values inside the fences.

questions.question_text: A dataset has a lower quartile of $Q_1 = 14$ and an upper quartile of $Q_3 = 26$. What is the maximum possible range of this dataset if it contains no outliers?

options.why: Reported the IQR ($26 - 14 = 12$) rather than the maximum possible range.
Quoted the upper fence ($44$) instead of calculating the difference between the upper and lower fences.
Calculated the difference between the upper fence and $Q_1$ ($44 - 14 = 30$) rather than subtracting the lower fence.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{IQR} = 26 - 14 = 12$
$\text{Lower fence} = 14 - 1.5 \times 12 = -4$
$\text{Upper fence} = 26 + 1.5 \times 12 = 44$
$\text{Max possible range} = \text{Upper fence} - \text{Lower fence}$
$= 44 - (-4)$
$= 48$

questions.question_text: A dataset of test scores has $Q_1 = 50, Q_3 = 70$, and contains an outlier at $x = 105$. If every score in the dataset is increased by $10$ marks, will the new score of $115$ still be an outlier?

options.text: Yes, because adding $10$ shifts both $Q_3$ and the upper fence by $10$ (new fence is $110$), so $115 > 110$ remains an outlier.
No, because $115$ exceeds the new fence of $110$ by only $5$, and an outlier must lie more than $1.5 \times \text{IQR} = 30$ beyond it.
options.why: A score is an outlier as soon as it exceeds the upper fence ($Q_3 + 1.5 \times \text{IQR}$); it does not need to exceed the fence by an additional $1.5 \times \text{IQR}$.

options.text: No, because adding 10 increases the IQR and widens the fences.
options.why: Adding a constant to all values does not change the IQR (spread remains identical).

options.text: Yes, because the upper fence remains fixed at 100 while the score increases to 115.
options.why: Adding 10 to every score shifts Q3 and the upper fence up by 10 as well.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{Original: } \text{IQR} = 70 - 50 = 20, \text{ Upper fence} = 70 + 1.5(20) = 100$
$\text{New: } Q_1 = 60, Q_3 = 80, \text{IQR} = 80 - 60 = 20$
$\text{New upper fence} = 80 + 1.5 \times 20 = 110$
Since $115 > 110$, $115$ remains an outlier.
